study.title: Deconvolution Analyses with Tent Functions Reveal Delayed and Long-sustained Increases of BOLD Signals with Acupuncture Stimulation
study.study_design: Block-design fMRI study with two parallel groups; one group received real acupuncture with manual manipulation, the other received both sham acupuncture (noninsertive) and scrubbing stimulation
study.population: 26 healthy right-handed adults (16 men, 10 women, aged 21 to 33 years)

conditions.timepoint_exact: during fMRI scan; four 15-s stimulation blocks (ON) interspersed between one 30-s and four 45-s rest blocks (OFF); total scanning time 270 s
conditions.scan_context: task-fMRI block design; stimulation performed inside scanner

conditions.condition_label_exact: Sham acupuncture (noninsertive); gentle tapping with 5.88 von Frey monofilament
conditions.timepoint_exact: during fMRI scan; four 15-s stimulation blocks (ON) interspersed between one 30-s and four 45-s rest blocks (OFF); total scanning time 270 s
conditions.scan_context: task-fMRI block design; stimulation performed inside scanner
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Explicitly noninsertive; a von Frey monofilament taps the skin surface at LI-4 without breaking the skin. No penetration occurs, placing this firmly at Level 3 (surface contact, no penetration).

conditions.condition_label_exact: Scrubbing stimulation (palm scrubbing with scrubbing sponge)
conditions.timepoint_exact: during fMRI scan; four 15-s stimulation blocks (ON) interspersed between one 30-s and four 45-s rest blocks (OFF); total scanning time 270 s
conditions.scan_context: task-fMRI block design; stimulation performed inside scanner
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Described as palm scrubbing with a scrubbing sponge — a noninsertive surface contact intervention. Despite inheriting some metadata fields from the von Frey condition (likely a data entry artifact), the condition label clearly describes skin-surface scrubbing with no penetration, consistent with Level 3. Confidence is medium rather than high because the metadata fields are inconsistent with the condition label, introducing minor uncertainty about the true protocol.

conditions.timepoint_exact: one 30-s and four 45-s rest blocks (OFF) within 270 s scan
conditions.scan_context: rest blocks within block design fMRI

funding_conflicts_registration.ethics_approval_exact: The ethics committee of the Meiji University of Integrative Medicine (Kyoto, Japan) approved the study, and subjects provided written consent after they were instructed regarding the type of stimulation.

extraction_notes.note: No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported in the paper for any activation cluster. The Table reports only region labels (Brodmann areas) and hemisphere (L, R, L·R, or —). No coordinate table with x/y/z values is provided.
No formal deqi or sensory rating scale (e.g., MASS, MGH Acupuncture Sensation Scale, VAS) was administered. Sensory responses are described only qualitatively in the Discussion section.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events are not reported or discussed.
Funding sources and conflicts of interest are not disclosed.
Trial registration number is not reported.
The paper does not explicitly state the coordinate space (MNI vs. Talairach). Given normalization to the MNI template, MNI is inferred but not confirmed.

The Table entry for Real acupuncture SI shows 'L·RL' which appears to be an OCR artifact. Based on context (real acupuncture activates SI bilaterally), 'L·R' is the most plausible reading. Extracted as 'L·R' in the cluster rows.
The Table entry for Real acupuncture SMA shows 'L·RL' which also appears to be an OCR artifact. Extracted as 'L·R' based on context.

The group design is described as two groups of 13, but it is unclear whether subjects were randomly allocated or assigned by another method. The paper states 'We divided the subjects' without specifying randomization.

The sham acupuncture and scrubbing conditions were administered to the same group of 13 subjects (within-subject for those 2 conditions), making the arm/condition distinction partially within-subject for arm_sham_scrub. The paper describes this as separate conditions within the same group.

Figure 3 shows beta amplitude time courses for all 8 brain regions with error bars and statistical markers, but the exact numeric values and all p-values from the ANOVA/t-test comparisons at each time point are not reported in text or tables. Results could only be extracted as ROI_summary narratives.
Figure 2 shows overlapped group statistical maps for each tent function but no peak coordinates are labeled or reported in the figure caption or text.

The paper does not report specific t-values or effect sizes for between-group or within-group IRF comparisons, only the qualitative direction of differences and significance markers visible in Figure 3.
Cluster sizes (in voxels or mm3) are not reported for any activation cluster beyond the threshold criterion of >10 voxels.

The tent function intervals: '1T represents 0 s, 2T represents 6 s' (caption Fig. 2). The 3T–5T functions correspond to the actual stimulation period (15 s blocks). Temporal estimates for activation peaks at '4T' and '6–8T' are thus approximately 18 s and 30–42 s after stimulus onset respectively. These are not explicitly stated but are derivable from the described TR=3000 ms and 2TR per tent interval.
